capsuleTopic.title: God
capsuleTopic.subtitle: Creator · covenant · presence · Father · judgment · mercy · final dwelling
capsuleTopic.orientation: Follow what Scripture says God does, says, permits, promises, judges, gives, and leaves unexplained. Keep poetry, narrative, law, prophecy, Gospel, letter, and vision distinct while tracing the relationships among God, Jesus, the Spirit, people, creation, and the nations.
capsuleTopic.trailPrompt: Notice divine action and speech, human response, the names and images used, and the tension each source preserves.

payload.description: Apostolic speech and final vision hold creation, judgment, Christ, love, and God’s dwelling together.

nodes.title: God speaks covenant commands

nodes.note: God tells Moses of Israel’s corruption, announces consuming wrath, and relents after Moses appeals to reputation and promise.
nodes.title: God threatens judgment and relents

nodes.note: The LORD passes before Moses and proclaims mercy, grace, patience, covenant love, faithfulness, forgiveness, and judgment.
nodes.title: God proclaims the divine name and character

payload.title: Name and deliverance

payload.description: Spirit, kingship, compassion, justice, waiting, restoration, and divine constancy face the future.

nodes.note: The LORD interprets the bones as Israel, commands prophecy, reunites bodies, gives breath, opens graves, and promises the Spirit and land.
nodes.title: God breathes life into dry bones

nodes.note: The Ancient of Days sits in fiery judgment, the court opens books, beasts lose dominion, and one like a son of man receives everlasting rule.
nodes.title: The Ancient of Days gives dominion

nodes.note: God recalls loving and teaching Israel, names their refusal, asks how to give them up, and says compassion grows warm.
nodes.title: God’s compassion interrupts destruction

nodes.note: The LORD’s day is warned as darkness, festivals and songs are rejected, and justice and righteousness are demanded like flowing water.
nodes.title: God rejects worship without justice

nodes.note: The prophetic exchange rejects escalating offerings as the answer and recalls what the LORD requires: justice, mercy, and humble walking with God.
nodes.title: God’s case narrows extravagant worship to faithful life

nodes.note: The prophet portrays God coming in splendor and judgment, remembers mighty acts, trembles, and chooses joy even when fields fail.
nodes.title: God’s terrifying advent becomes the ground of trust

nodes.note: The LORD expresses jealous concern for Zion, promises to return, renames Jerusalem by truth and holiness, gathers people, and renews covenant belonging.
nodes.title: God returns to dwell in a truthful city

nodes.note: The LORD announces a messenger and sudden coming, compares the arrival to refining fire, purifies worship, judges oppression, and grounds survival in divine constancy.
nodes.title: The unchanging God comes to refine and judge

payload.title: Future and faithfulness

payload.description: Jesus’ birth, prayer, teaching, suffering, commission, and the Word reshape how God is named.

nodes.note: The child is conceived from the Holy Spirit, named Jesus because he will save his people from sins, and identified through Isaiah’s “God with us.”
nodes.title: God is named in Jesus’ conception and mission

nodes.note: Jesus is baptized, heaven opens, God’s Spirit descends, and a heavenly voice names the beloved Son and delight.
nodes.title: Father, Son, and Spirit appear at baptism

nodes.note: Jesus directs disciples to a Father who knows needs, gives a shared prayer, and ties received and extended forgiveness together.
nodes.title: Jesus teaches prayer to the Father

nodes.note: Jesus addresses the Father as Lord of heaven and earth, says mutual knowledge belongs uniquely to Father and Son, and invites the weary to himself.
nodes.title: Jesus thanks the Father and offers rest

nodes.note: A bright cloud overshadows Jesus, Moses, and Elijah; the voice repeats beloved Son language and commands the disciples to listen to him.
nodes.title: The voice identifies the beloved Son

nodes.note: Jesus addresses “my God” in abandonment, cries again, dies, and is followed by torn curtain, earthquake, opened tombs, and the centurion’s confession.
nodes.title: Jesus cries to God and dies

nodes.note: The risen Jesus claims all authority, sends disciples to all nations, commands baptism in the singular name of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and promises presence.
nodes.title: Jesus commissions in one shared name

nodes.note: The prologue distinguishes the Word as with God, calls the Word God, attributes creation and life to him, and says the Word became flesh and made the unseen God known.
nodes.title: The Word is with God and is God

payload.title: Jesus names the Father

payload.description: John’s Gospel and Pentecost press on sending, authority, unity, seeing, worship, prayer, and Spirit.

nodes.note: God’s love gives the only Son for life, sends him not to condemn but to save, while judgment appears through response to light.
nodes.title: God loves and sends the Son

nodes.note: Jesus says the Father works, the Son sees and does the Father’s works, gives life, receives judgment authority, and is to be honored as the Father.
nodes.title: The Son does what the Father does

nodes.note: Jesus honors the Father, promises life to those keeping his word, and closes the dispute by saying, “Before Abraham came into existence, I am.”
nodes.title: Jesus says “I am” before Abraham

nodes.note: Jesus describes shared keeping of the sheep, says he and the Father are one, and defends his claim through works and Scripture.
nodes.title: Jesus says he and the Father are one

nodes.note: Jesus names himself as way, truth, and life, says knowing him means knowing the Father, and speaks of mutual indwelling through words and works.
nodes.title: Seeing Jesus is tied to seeing the Father

nodes.note: Jesus addresses the Father, speaks of shared glory before the world, gives eternal life through knowing Father and Son, and asks for protected, sanctified unity.
nodes.title: Jesus prays to the Father about glory and unity

nodes.note: The risen Jesus offers Thomas the requested wounds and calls him from unbelief to belief.
nodes.title: Thomas addresses Jesus as Lord and God

nodes.note: Wind, fire, languages, and prophetic speech mark the Spirit’s arrival, which Peter interprets through God’s promise to pour out the Spirit on all kinds of people.
nodes.title: God pours out the Spirit

payload.title: Jesus and God

payload.description: Foreigners, empires, heavenly assemblies, wisdom, judgment, and mercy widen the field.

nodes.note: The God of Israel heals Naaman through Elisha’s simple instruction and receives the foreigner’s confession.
nodes.title: God heals a foreign commander

nodes.note: The LORD is addressed as creator and enthroned God, answers the Assyrian boast, promises Jerusalem’s deliverance, and strikes the camp.
nodes.title: God answers Assyria’s challenge

nodes.note: The God of the ancestors repeatedly sends messengers, gives the people over after sustained rejection, and later stirs Cyrus to rebuild.
nodes.title: God warns, judges, and stirs return

nodes.note: God commends Job and sets limits on the accuser’s power while permitting devastating loss.
nodes.title: God permits Job’s testing in the heavenly court

nodes.note: The LORD questions Job about earth, sea, dawn, death, and the world’s breadth rather than first explaining Job’s suffering.
nodes.title: God answers Job from the whirlwind

nodes.note: God stands in an assembly, rebukes unjust rulers called gods, and announces that they will die like humans.
nodes.title: God judges in the divine assembly

nodes.note: The writer says God can act with great power yet orders all things by measure and shows mercy because all belong to God.
nodes.title: God’s power is described through measure and mercy

nodes.note: The sage says human speech cannot finish naming God, whose works exceed praise and whose greatness is beyond tracing.
nodes.title: Praise reaches the limit of speech

payload.title: Judgment, exile, and the nations

payload.description: God accompanies Israel, speaks through prophets, answers prayer, and challenges royal power.

nodes.note: The LORD promises presence, land, and success tied to courage and careful attention to the instruction.
nodes.title: God commissions Joshua

nodes.note: The LORD’s anger gives Israel into enemies, mercy raises judges, and judgment tests the nations when Israel repeatedly turns away.
nodes.title: God responds to Israel’s recurring abandonment

nodes.note: The LORD calls Samuel, confirms judgment on Eli’s house, and establishes Samuel as a trustworthy prophet.
nodes.title: God calls Samuel in a time of rare words

nodes.note: The LORD tells Samuel that Israel has rejected divine kingship, orders a warning, and finally tells him to appoint a king.
nodes.title: God interprets Israel’s demand for a king

nodes.note: The LORD recalls moving in a tent, rejects David’s proposed temple role, and promises David a house, son, kingdom, and enduring throne.
nodes.title: God refuses David’s house and promises one

nodes.note: Solomon praises covenant faithfulness and asks God to hear prayers directed toward the temple across sin, defeat, drought, exile, and foreign prayer.
nodes.title: Solomon addresses the God heaven cannot contain

nodes.note: The LORD answers Elijah’s prayer with fire that consumes offering, wood, stones, dust, and water.
nodes.title: God answers Elijah by fire

nodes.note: The LORD questions Elijah, passes by amid wind, earthquake, and fire, speaks in a low sound, and gives new assignments and a preserved remnant.
nodes.title: God questions Elijah and speaks after the storm

payload.title: Land, judges, and kings

payload.description: God creates, addresses human beings, judges violence, preserves life, and limits human ambition.

nodes.note: God creates the heavens and earth, speaks light into darkness, and names day and night.
nodes.title: God creates and speaks light

nodes.note: God deliberates, makes humankind in the divine image, blesses them, and gives them rule and food.
nodes.title: God makes humanity in God’s image

nodes.note: The LORD God forms the man from dust, breathes life, plants a garden, and causes trees to grow.
nodes.title: God forms and plants

nodes.note: God calls to the hiding humans, questions them, announces consequences, clothes them, and bars the tree of life.
nodes.title: God seeks, questions, judges, and clothes

nodes.note: God questions Cain, warns about sin, names Abel’s blood as a witness, judges Cain, and marks him against vengeance.
nodes.title: God warns Cain and hears blood

nodes.note: God sees pervasive evil, grieves, announces destruction, and gives Noah detailed instructions for preservation.
nodes.title: God grieves violence and preserves Noah

nodes.note: God receives Noah’s offering, promises not to strike every living thing again, blesses life, and gives the rainbow as covenant sign.
nodes.title: God limits judgment and sets the bow

nodes.note: The LORD comes down, assesses the city and tower, confuses speech, and scatters the builders.
nodes.title: God descends and scatters Babel

payload.title: Maker and the early world

payload.description: Poetry speaks to and about God through praise, grief, confession, trust, knowledge, and time.

nodes.note: The psalm addresses the LORD’s majestic name, recalls the heavens as divine work, and marvels that God remembers and appoints humans.
nodes.title: God’s majesty and human vocation

nodes.note: The heavens declare God’s glory without audible speech, while the LORD’s instruction speaks clearly, restores, warns, and exposes hidden faults.
nodes.title: Creation and instruction disclose God differently

nodes.note: The speaker addresses God as absent and silent, remembers earlier trust, asks for rescue, and anticipates praise among nations and future generations.
nodes.title: The absent God becomes the God of praise

nodes.note: The LORD is named as shepherd who provides, restores, guides, accompanies through death-shadow, hosts, anoints, and gives enduring welcome.
nodes.title: The LORD shepherds through danger

nodes.note: God is addressed as merciful judge who can wash, create a clean heart, renew a spirit, restore joy, and receive truthful sacrifice.
nodes.title: God is asked to cleanse and recreate

nodes.note: The LORD forgives, heals, rescues, judges for the oppressed, reveals ways to Moses, shows compassion, and remembers human dust.
nodes.title: God’s mercy is measured against human frailty

nodes.note: The LORD knows speech and movement, is present across height and depth, forms life in the womb, and is invited to search the speaker.
nodes.title: God knows, surrounds, and examines

nodes.note: God is said to make everything fitting in its time, place eternity in human hearts, give work and enjoyment, and act enduringly.
nodes.title: God gives time and limits human grasp

payload.title: Prayer and wisdom

payload.description: Glory, holiness, atonement, blessing, Spirit, rebellion, and loyalty shape life near God.

nodes.note: The cloud covers the tent, the LORD’s glory fills it, and the cloud or fire directs Israel’s journeys.
nodes.title: Glory fills the tabernacle

nodes.note: The LORD’s glory appears and fire consumes the offering on the altar.
nodes.title: Fire comes from before the LORD

nodes.note: The LORD regulates Aaron’s entrance, offerings, incense, blood, and the two goats for atonement and removal of sins.
nodes.title: God provides guarded approach and removal

nodes.note: The LORD gives words by which priests place the divine name on Israel: blessing, keeping, light, grace, attention, and peace.
nodes.title: God places the name in blessing

nodes.note: The LORD takes from the Spirit on Moses and places it on seventy elders, including two who remain in the camp.
nodes.title: God shares the Spirit among elders

nodes.note: The LORD charges Israel with unbelief, threatens destruction, hears Moses’ appeal, pardons, and still bars the rebellious generation from the land.
nodes.title: God judges unbelief and hears intercession

nodes.note: The LORD instructs Moses to speak to the rock, gives water, and says Moses and Aaron failed to believe and sanctify him.
nodes.title: God gives water and judges leaders

nodes.note: The command names the LORD as Israel’s God, calls for whole-person love, and places the words through daily life.
nodes.title: Israel hears that the LORD is one

payload.title: Presence in the wilderness

payload.description: God calls, promises, tests, meets, wrestles, and works through family histories.

nodes.note: The LORD commands Abram to leave and promises land, nation, blessing, and a wider blessing through him.
nodes.title: God calls Abram away

nodes.note: God answers Abram’s fear and childlessness, counts faith as righteousness, and binds the land promise through a covenant sign.
nodes.title: God promises descendants and land

nodes.note: God identifies himself as God Almighty, renames Abram, promises descendants and land, and commands circumcision.
nodes.title: God names covenant and sign

nodes.note: The LORD chooses to disclose the outcry against Sodom and allows Abraham’s repeated appeal concerning the righteous and wicked.
nodes.title: God discloses judgment to Abraham

nodes.note: God commands the offering of Isaac, stops Abraham’s hand, provides a ram, and renews the promise.
nodes.title: God tests Abraham over Isaac

nodes.note: The LORD stands above the stairway, repeats the ancestral promise, and promises presence and return.
nodes.title: God meets Jacob in flight

nodes.note: A mysterious man wrestles Jacob, wounds him, renames him Israel, and blesses him.
nodes.title: God meets Jacob in struggle

nodes.note: Joseph distinguishes his brothers’ evil intention from God’s intention to preserve many lives.
nodes.title: Joseph names God’s purpose in human evil

payload.title: Promise and the patriarchs

payload.description: Prophets encounter holiness, announce judgment, name God’s purposes, and hold out renewal.

nodes.note: The Lord sits high on a throne, is acclaimed as holy, shakes the thresholds, cleanses Isaiah, and asks whom to send.
nodes.title: The Holy One commissions Isaiah

nodes.note: The LORD measures creation, has no instructor or equal, rules nations, names the stars, and gives strength to the weary.
nodes.title: God is incomparable and attends the weary

nodes.note: The LORD calls Cyrus anointed, subdues nations, names and equips him, declares sole deity, and claims light, darkness, well-being, and calamity.
nodes.title: God calls Cyrus without being known by him

nodes.note: The LORD calls the wicked to return for abundant pardon and compares the divine word to rain that accomplishes its purpose.
nodes.title: God’s higher ways and effective word

nodes.note: The LORD commands amended ways, condemns oppression and idolatry, and warns that the house bearing the divine name can be treated like Shiloh.
nodes.title: God rejects confidence in the temple

nodes.note: The LORD promises a new covenant unlike the broken exodus covenant, writes instruction on hearts, renews belonging, spreads knowledge, and forgives sin.
nodes.title: God promises instruction written within

nodes.note: Above the living beings and platform, Ezekiel sees a throne, a human-like figure, fire, brightness, and rainbow likeness called the LORD’s glory.
nodes.title: Glory appears in human likeness and fire

nodes.note: The Lord GOD says restoration is not for Israel’s sake, sanctifies the profaned name, gathers, cleanses, gives a new heart and Spirit, and produces obedience.
nodes.title: God acts for the holy name and renews Israel

payload.title: The prophetic voice
